name: Rocket Car Parts
summary: Rocket Car Parts are the scattered, twisted metal remains of high-speed collisions across the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Constantly generated by reckless gnome and goblin racers pushing experimental speeders past their limits, these salvaged scraps are harvested by opportunists looking to turn racetrack accidents into quick coin.

sections.title: Speed, Wrecks, and Shrewd Commerce
sections.body: The Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats is the staging ground for an unending, combustible rivalry between goblin and gnome engineering. In their pursuit of unmatched land speed, racers regularly suffer catastrophic breakdowns, explosive misfires, and high-velocity crashes that scatter metal across the salt flats. These discarded remnants—ranging from bent cylinders and burnt gears to crushed sheet metal—do not stay abandoned for long. Scavengers and merchants, most notably the opportunistic dwarf Kravel Koalbeard, hire passing adventurers to comb the blinding white expanse and collect the debris. Because both racing teams are perpetually desperate for spare machinery to patch together their next prototype, scavenged wreckage can easily be resold directly back to the very teams that wrecked it.

faq.q: Where do all these rocket car parts come from?
aliases: why are there parts on the salt flats
where do the parts come from
faq.answer: They are the aftermath of constant crashes, explosions, and mechanical failures at the Mirage Raceway. Gnome and goblin pilots routinely push volatile, experimental rocket-powered vehicles to destruction across the vast salt flats of Thousand Needles.

Merchants like the dwarf Kravel Koalbeard collect the wreckage from wanderers and turn around to sell the salvaged gears, plating, and gizmos back to the gnomes and goblins, who always need spare materials to repair and enhance their racing cars.

faq.q: Are the parts dangerous to scavenge?
aliases: is it safe to pick up parts
faq.answer: The debris itself is inert wreckage, though occasionally bearing grim signs of violent crashes like severed appendages pinched in the metal. The primary danger comes from the salt flats' hostile wildlife, including basilisks, scorched scorpids, and predatory salt vultures that prowl around the debris fields.

faq.q: Do the gnomes and goblins care that the parts are from crashed cars?
faq.answer: Not in the slightest. Neither gnome nor goblin competitors are squeamish about recycled materials. Their sole priority is securing workable contraptions, gears, and metal plating to assemble fast enough to outrun each other on the track.

angles.text: The litter of burnt gears and mangled exhaust assemblies across the salt flats serves as a testament to the chaotic extremes of gnome and goblin engineering philosophy.
While gnomes and goblins care only for the race itself, enterprising dwarves like Kravel Koalbeard prove that the real profit lies in scavenging the wreckage left in their wake.
